places.name: Tower Bridge
places.description: Victorian Gothic bascule bridge spanning the Thames since 1894. Twin towers rise 65m. The bridge still opens 800+ times a year for tall river traffic. Glass-floor walkway 42m above water.
highlights: Opens 800+ times annually for tall ships

places.name: Borough Market
places.description: London's oldest food market, trading since at least the 12th century. Artisan cheeses, sourdough, Ethiopian coffee, and Neal's Yard dairy. The city's culinary soul under Victorian ironwork.

places.name: The British Museum
places.description: World's largest collection of human history and culture — 8 million objects. Rosetta Stone, Elgin Marbles, Egyptian mummies, Sutton Hoo helmet. Norman Foster Great Court atrium.

places.name: St Paul's Cathedral
places.description: Sir Christopher Wren's Baroque masterpiece, completed 1710. Dome 111m high, whispering gallery, and Gold Gallery with panoramic City views. Survived the Blitz, host to Churchill's funeral.

places.name: Tate Modern
places.description: World's most visited modern art museum in a converted Bankside Power Station. Turbine Hall installations, Picasso, Warhol, Rothko. Blavatnik Building extension with panoramic terrace.

places.name: Hyde Park
places.description: 142 hectares of royal parkland at the heart of London. Serpentine lake, Speakers' Corner, Rose Garden and Diana Memorial Fountain. Winter Wonderland at Christmas.

places.name: Shoreditch — Brick Lane
places.description: East London's creative epicentre. Banksy murals, vintage shops, Bangladeshi curry houses on Brick Lane, and the Sunday Up Market. Gentrification meets Bengali heritage.

places.name: Dishoom Carnaby
places.description: Homage to Bombay's Irani cafés, open since 2010. House black daal simmered 24 hours, bacon naan roll, salli boti. Queue or book weeks ahead — London's most-loved Indian.
highlights: Queue before opening or book weeks ahead
